solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Papa courting flying officer in RAF (5,7)

indicators.note: the letters fly apart and land in a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: A father is romancing a pilot who serves in the Royal Air Force.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying officer' looks like one RAF rank, but 'flying' is the instruction and the rank wanted is a higher one.
annotation.definitionFit: A group captain is a senior commissioned rank in the Royal Air Force.

entries.clue: Reliable choice of cannabis for degenerate (2,2,3)

blocks.note: a go-to is the option you can always rely on

annotation.surface: Someone's dependable pick of drugs suits a person who has gone to the bad.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' reads as a noun, a wastrel, but it is the verb: to decline.
annotation.definitionFit: To go to pot is to deteriorate or fall into ruin.

entries.clue: Injured hero and vet totter up without a prescription (4-3-7)

indicators.note: HERO and VET are damaged into a new order

blocks.note: one who tots up a sum is a counter

annotation.surface: A wounded hero and an animal doctor stagger to their feet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Totter up' suggests staggering upright; read it as 'totter-up', someone who tots up figures.
annotation.definitionFit: Over-the-counter medicines are sold without needing a doctor's prescription.

entries.clue: Blubber of whales possibly source of green energy (5)

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a group of whales is a pod; 'possibly' because other animals form pods too
E is the symbol for energy

annotation.surface: Whale blubber might be a source of renewable energy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blubber of whales' reads as one phrase; only 'Blubber', meaning body fat, is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Podge is informal British for excess body fat.

entries.clue: Records playful American composer (8)

blocks.note: an arch look is playfully knowing

annotation.surface: Someone records a light-hearted American composer's music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Records' looks like a verb or vinyl discs in a musical surface; it is the noun for stored documents.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: archives are the stored documents of an institution, kept as its records.

entries.clue: Asian band on the radio (4)

indicators.note: a radio carries only sound, so the word is heard not seen

blocks.note: a tie is a band or strip; say it and you have the nationality

annotation.surface: A group of Asian musicians is being played on the radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Band' pretends to be a pop group because of 'radio'; it is a strip that ties.
annotation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, in Asia.

entries.clue: Passionately arouse befuddled auntie drinking stout (9)

indicators.note: AUNTIE's letters are muddled
the rearranged AUNTIE takes FAT inside

annotation.surface: A tipsy aunt knocking back a pint of stout gets rather amorous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the dark beer she is drinking; it is the adjective meaning plump.
annotation.definitionFit: To infatuate is to inspire an intense, foolish passion in someone.

entries.clue: Educated elite and liberal A-list get in line (14)

indicators.note: a free, loose treatment of the letters

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to be rearranged

annotation.surface: The educated, the liberal and the celebrity class all have to queue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' sits in a list of kinds of people, looking like part of the set; it is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes via Russian for the intellectual class that shapes a nation's culture.

entries.clue: Quietly knowledgeable about subatomic particle (6)

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

annotation.surface: Someone quietly clever about particle physics.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the photon is the quantum of light, one of the particles smaller than an atom.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knowledgeable' gives HOT in the informal sense of well versed, as in 'hot on the rules'.

entries.clue: Reportedly glowing after toddler’s first step (5)

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word goes by its sound
the first letter of 'toddler'
the sound-alike comes after T

blocks.note: glowing coals are red; READ in the past tense is said the same way

annotation.surface: Parents beam proudly at a toddler's first step.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Glowing' reads as proud parents; it is red-hot. 'Step' is the definition, not part of the toddler story.
annotation.definitionFit: A tread is a step, or the flat part of a stair you step on.

entries.clue: Singer teasing short companion (9)

indicators.note: CHAFFING is cut short by its last letter

blocks.note: CHAFFING (teasing banter) without its final G
CH = Companion of Honour, a British order

annotation.surface: A vocalist ribbing a friend who is not very tall.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like it describes the companion; it trims 'teasing'. 'Singer' is a songbird, not a vocalist.
annotation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch known for its song.

entries.clue: Regularly sent niece on way, arousing pity (8)

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at every second step
in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

annotation.surface: Sending your niece off on her travels is a sad sight.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads the whole as a farewell; the chunks are assembled in the opposite order to the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Pathetic means evoking pity or sadness.

entries.clue: Asleep in theatre stalls (2,4)

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the next words

annotation.surface: Someone dozing off in the stalls during a play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stalls' could be a verb, but here it is the ground-floor seats and simply holds the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: At rest means sleeping or not moving.

entries.clue: Support and worry about backward adolescent (8)

indicators.note: backward means facing the wrong way, so the letters of RE are read in reverse

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball
to nag is to worry at someone
RE means about, as in memo headings

annotation.surface: Parents support and fret over a child who is slow to develop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backward adolescent' reads as a slow child, but 'backward' turns RE round and 'adolescent' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A teenager is an adolescent aged thirteen to nineteen.

entries.clue: Article with suggestion regarding Italian food (9)

annotation.surface: A magazine article offering tips on Italian cooking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' pretends to be a piece of journalism; it is just AN.
annotation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian starter course of cold meats and vegetables.

entries.clue: Everyone in Slough is lost (6)

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so ALL goes within FEN

blocks.note: a slough is a bog; so is a fen

annotation.surface: Everybody in the town of Slough has lost their way.
annotation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, so the capital hides the plain word for a swamp.
annotation.definitionFit: The fallen are those lost in battle; fallen means killed or lost.

entries.clue: Detectives covering murder (8)

annotation.surface: Police detectives are reporting on a killing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covering' looks like reporting on the case; it is a noun, a patch.
annotation.definitionFit: To dispatch someone is to kill them quickly.

entries.clue: Extremely frail, like porridge to be light (6)

indicators.note: take the extreme ends of FRAIL

annotation.surface: Someone very weak is told porridge will leave them feeling light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Light' is the definition of a floaty fabric or feeling, not light in weight after a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: Floaty describes something light and airy, like a floaty dress.

entries.clue: Agent in favour of restraining statute (6)

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold something in check, so FOR holds ACT inside it

blocks.note: an Act of Parliament is a statute

annotation.surface: A spy who supports limiting the law.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Agent' suggests a spy; a factor is a business agent.
annotation.definitionFit: A factor is an agent who buys or sells on someone else's behalf.

entries.clue: Appallingly heartless Edinburgh mercenary (5,3)

indicators.note: the middle letter B of EDINBURGH is removed
the remaining letters are rearranged badly

annotation.surface: A soldier-for-hire from Edinburgh with no heart at all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' reads as cruelty; it removes the central letter of the city name.
annotation.definitionFit: A hired gun is someone paid to fight or kill for others.

entries.clue: Candidate originally called to get old minister on board (7)

indicators.note: NEE gets the other letters
a passenger on board is inside the vessel, so the letters are carried inside NEE

blocks.note: née means 'born as', a woman's original name
MINISTER cut short to its first three letters

annotation.surface: An election candidate was first asked to bring an old politician into the team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Originally' looks like a first-letter instruction; 'originally called' is NEE, as in 'Mrs Smith, née Jones'.
annotation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward as a candidate.

entries.clue: Naked Dane bitten by ape in treetops (6)

indicators.note: DANE is stripped of its outer letters
the ape's mouth closes round AN

annotation.surface: A nude Dane is nipped by a monkey up in the jungle trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ape' is the verb, to imitate, not the animal that fits the jungle picture.
annotation.definitionFit: The canopy is the upper layer of a forest formed by treetops.

entries.clue: Antelope cutting thigh on edges of stump in moss (8)

indicators.note: a thing cutting into another pushes into its middle, so GNU splits HAM
in an across clue, HAGNUM follows SP
the edges of STUMP are its outer letters

blocks.note: the ham is the back of the thigh
the gnu is an African antelope

annotation.surface: An antelope grazes a leg on a tree stump in a mossy wood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stump' feels like a tree stump in the scene; only its outside letters are used.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by genus: sphagnum is the peat or bog moss, used by gardeners and in peat formation.

entries.clue: Camerawoman from India ejected from jet (5)

indicators.note: I is thrown out of AIRBUS

blocks.note: an Airbus is a jet airliner
I is India in the NATO alphabet; it is removed

annotation.surface: A camerawoman from India is thrown off a plane.
annotation.walkthrough: Diane Arbus was an American photographer. 'From India' suggests where she comes from; it is the letter to lose.
annotation.definitionFit: Diane Arbus was a celebrated twentieth-century American photographer.

entries.clue: Stuck-up urchin wanting cake and jelly (4)

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the urchin is short of the cake
in a down clue, sticking up puts the letters in reverse

blocks.note: a ragamuffin is a scruffy child
a muffin is a small cake; it is removed

annotation.surface: A snooty street child turns down cake and jelly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuck-up' reads as snobbish; in a down entry it means written upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Agar is a jelly made from seaweed, used in cooking and labs.

entries.clue: Lovers might lose heads and control (9)

indicators.note: both words lose their first letters

annotation.surface: Lovers may lose their heads and all self-control.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a romantic cliché; 'heads' is literal, the first letters of the two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Oversight means supervision, having control over something.

entries.clue: Bowl sailor over with lust? (5)

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so the sailor's letters are flipped

blocks.note: lust is one of the seven deadly sins

annotation.surface: A sailor is bowled over by desire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bowl ... over' looks like a phrasal verb; 'Bowl' is the noun definition and 'over' reverses the sailor.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a basin is a wide open bowl for washing or mixing.

entries.clue: Leader of union framed by pro-government journalists (6,6)

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the letter sits inside the phrase like a picture in a frame

blocks.note: for the state = on the government's side

annotation.surface: A trade union boss is stitched up by journalists loyal to the government.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Framed' reads as falsely accused, the sort of story the press tells; here it means enclosed.
annotation.definitionFit: The fourth estate is the press, seen as a power alongside the traditional estates of the realm.
